theory.intro: The **maximum flow** of a network is the greatest amount that can travel from the source to the sink. It is found by pushing flow along one source-to-sink path at a time until the edges run out of spare capacity.
facts: An edge is **saturated** when its remaining capacity reaches $0$, so it can carry nothing more.
After a path is used, subtract its flow from the remaining capacity of every edge on that path.
The maximum flow is the **sum of the path flows**, not the sum of the capacities leaving the source.
A path that contains a saturated edge can carry no extra flow, so it is skipped.
Work through the paths systematically, such as top to bottom, so that no path is missed.
The order the paths are taken in changes the leftover capacities but never changes the maximum flow.
The number left on each edge at the end is that edge's unused capacity.
steps: List every path from the source to the sink
Find the smallest remaining capacity on the path
Subtract that flow from every edge on the path
Add the path flows to give the maximum flow
